source.title: How Post-Training Reshapes LLMs: A Mechanistic View on Knowledge, Truthfulness, Refusal, and Confidence
source.authors: Hongzhe Du; Weikai Li; Min Cai; Karim Saraipour; Zimin Zhang; Himabindu Lakkaraju; Yizhou Sun; Shichang Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study learns refusal directions by contrasting harmful and harmless prompts and applies addition and ablation interventions, closely matching the original method, on additional model families and post-training stages.
record.gate_note: Refusal intervention scores are reported for harmful and harmless prompts. The paper also reports refusal-direction cosine comparisons, but the figure does not provide a clear enough mapping of values to include as numerical rows. Results for adding directions on harmful prompts and ablating directions on harmless prompts are not included as rows because the claim versions specify adding to harmless requests and removing refusals to harmful requests.
record.test_reason: The study extracts difference-in-means refusal directions (advbench minus alpaca) following Arditi et al. It ablates them at all layers and adds them at one layer in base, SFT and instruct models of Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-2-13B, Qwen-1.5-0.5B and Gemma-2-9B. It reports keyword refusal scores for native and cross-stage directions, so its results bear on V1, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors conclude that post-training changes the refusal direction (low BASE–POST cosine similarity), so BASE directions transfer poorly forward to SFT/INSTRUCT. They assert that backward transfer (POST→BASE) works, but this rests on Kissane et al. and reports no numbers of its own; the record should not present it as a result of this study. They flag BASE→SFT addition (0.85) as an anomaly and speculate that DPO reduced the instruct model's latent refusal tendency.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses harmful-minus-harmless mean activation differences and tests direction addition and ablation across layers and token positions. Its refusal score is based on refusal keywords at the beginning of outputs; addition uses a selected layer, and direction extraction layer/token choices vary by model.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model and training stage; the paper reports different extraction layer and token-position choices across models (Appendix D.3, Table 15).
record.problems: The refusal measure is a keyword-based score, not a broader semantic refusal assessment. The main Llama-3.1-8B intervention evaluation samples 100 prompts per input category, and the learned contrastive direction uses size-128 subsets. General capability after ablation/addition was not evaluated, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted addition results on harmful prompts and ablation results on harmless prompts from Tables 4, 16, 17, and 22 because the claim versions concern addition to harmless requests and removal of refusals to harmful requests. The refusal-direction cosine comparison in Figure 3 is described as very low for BASE versus post-trained directions, but no separate row was recorded because the figure's values are not reliably assignable from the provided text.

untested.parts: Preservation of general capabilities after ablation or addition was not measured.
Cross-language transfer was not tested. INSTRUCT→BASE (backward) transfer is asserted in the text but no numbers are reported.
No controlled manipulation of training data, algorithm or timing. The comparison is across released checkpoints (Tulu SFT vs. official instruct), and the DPO explanation is speculative.

missing.what: Cosine similarity of refusal directions in Llama-3.1-8B: BASE–SFT 0.147, BASE–INSTRUCT 0.252, SFT–INSTRUCT 0.660. The values are readable, contrary to rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: Refusal is scored by keywords at the start of outputs, on 100 sampled prompts with no uncertainty reported, so small differences (e.g. R1, R12, R16, R21) are fragile. The SFT checkpoint is an external Tulu model, not part of the official Llama pipeline. The native-direction instruct results replicate the original.

versions.untested_parts: Whether general capabilities are largely preserved after the refusal interventions was not measured.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration procedure was evaluated.
No jailbreak attack or training against refusal-direction ablation was tested.
The study compares directions across models but does not test whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or distributed across multiple directions within a model.
The study does not separate harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
Transfer across languages was not tested; model-variant and base-to-post-trained transfer were tested.
The study compares base, SFT, and instruct stages, but does not isolate the causal effects of specific training data, algorithms, or timing.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Base vs SFT vs instruct checkpoints, Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-2-13B
labels.reason: Removability rises with stage (R1, R3, R7; R21 vs R22). The reason omits R22: Llama-2-13B-Instruct ablation is 0.99->0.59, not clean. Checkpoints are observational; the SFT is external Tulu-3.

relation.reason: Its own intervention results (Tables 4, 16, 17, 22) bear on V1, V6 and V7.

tranche.reason: Like Arditi et al., the study uses difference-in-means directions (advbench minus alpaca), all-layer ablation, addition at a chosen layer and a keyword refusal score.

source_check.notes: Code is public (abstract: HZD01/post-training-mechanistic-analysis); the record says code n. There is no random-direction control (the only comparisons are unintervened baselines and native vs transferred directions), no capability check and no uncertainty. The SFT model is the external Tulu-3 SFT, and base models use constructed templates. The paper's 'backward transfer works' claim rests on Kissane et al., not on its own numbers.

statements.correction: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct 0.98->0.01 and 0.0->1.0 (Table 4). Qwen-1.5-0.5B-chat 0.85->0.04 and 0.03->0.68. Gemma-2-9B-it 0.98->0.00 and 0.02->0.75 (Tables 16-17, n not stated). No capability check, no random-direction control.
statements.problem: Minor: the 100-sampled-prompts condition is stated only for the Llama-3.1-8B experiments; Appendix D.5 gives no n for Qwen/Gemma. Qwen 0.68 and Gemma 0.75 addition are clearly incomplete.

statements.correction: Addition is applied at all token positions at the best-performing layer (Section 6).
The study reports no base self-intervention for Qwen-1.5-0.5B or Gemma-2-9B, only their BASE directions applied to INSTRUCT.
Cite R1, R2, R3, R4 for this study.
statements.problem: Row ids cited (R1, R2, R22) don't match: the SFT numbers are R3/R4, and R22 isn't used in the text.

statements.correction: BASE->SFT addition 0.01->0.85 is base-to-SFT transfer; Appendix D.4 calls it abnormal; BASE->SFT ablation leaves 0.99 (R5); authors conclude rBASE generally can't steer SFT or INSTRUCT.
statements.problem: The heading ('post-training checkpoints into instruct, chat into base') doesn't fit R6, which is BASE->SFT. Also omits that the authors call 0.85 an abnormal case.

statements.correction: Confirmed: the study reports no POST->BASE refusal numbers; Section 6 attributes backward transfer to Kissane et al.
Figure 3c: rBASE has very low cosine similarity with rSFT and rINSTRUCT for Llama-3.1-8B.
statements.problem: Could add that the study also reports low BASE-vs-SFT/INSTRUCT cosine (Figure 3c, figure only).

statements.correction: Llama-2-13B-Instruct own-direction ablation 0.99->0.59 (Table 22): the instruct stage is only partly removable there. Refusal families: Llama (3.1-8B, 2-13B), Qwen-1.5, Gemma-2.
statements.problem: Omits the Llama-2-13B-Instruct stage point (0.99->0.59, R22) though its conditions list Llama-2-13B Instruct. Refusal experiments span three families, not four (Mistral is used only for other perspectives).

statements.correction: Tables 16-17 cover only INSTRUCT models with INS or BASE directions. Du also prompts base models with constructed templates (Appendix D.2).
statements.problem: 'Not shown in the pack' understates it: the study does not report base self-direction results for Qwen/Gemma at all.

statements.correction: Code: HZD01/post-training-mechanistic-analysis (abstract). All numbers are correct.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Native directions on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen-1.5-0.5B-chat, Gemma-2-9B-it, and the reported Llama-2-13B-Instruct harmless-input condition
reader_labels.reason: Native-direction interventions strongly reduced harmful-input refusal or induced harmless-input refusal in these tested conditions (R7, R10, R13, R14, R24).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: SFT self-ablation and Llama-2-13B-Instruct harmful-input self-ablation
reader_labels.reason: Ablation reduced refusal but left substantial refusal scores, rather than removing refusal nearly completely (R3, R22).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The harmful-input refusal score increased after the direction was ablated (R21).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: BASE-to-SFT transfer on harmless prompts in the Llama-3.1-8B family
reader_labels.reason: The BASE direction increased the SFT model's harmless-input refusal score from 0.01 to 0.85 (R6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: BASE-to-INSTRUCT transfer across tested model families and training stages
reader_labels.reason: Transfer often failed or was weaker than the native direction, though some conditions showed partial effects (R5, R8, R9, R12, R15, R16, R19, R20, R23, R25).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Comparisons among BASE, SFT, and INSTRUCT refusal directions in the tested Llama-3.1-8B family
reader_labels.reason: Effectiveness differed by training stage: the BASE direction transferred strongly to SFT harmless inputs but poorly to INSTRUCT, while native INSTRUCT ablation was effective (R6, R7, R9, R12).
